value.same_fcc_id: 47 CFR 2.924: the grantee may market electrically identical devices under different trade names and model numbers on the same FCC ID without new authorization. A rebrand by anyone other than the grantee must be done by, or with authorization of, the grantee under 2.933 (new application for a change in FCC ID if we want our own ID: original ID, grant date, statement of no change, new label photos). Practical path: factory marks our private-label unit with its own FCC ID and gives a written letter that the unit is electrically identical to the granted model.
value.how_to_check: FCC ID search (fcc.gov/oet/ea/fccid, fccid.io): confirm the grantee code and model on the label, the frequency bands (2.4 vs 5 GHz Wi-Fi both listed), the internal photos match the sample, and the grant is active.
value.sdoc_vs_certification: Wi-Fi radio = intentional radiator, so needs Certification (FCC ID via a TCB). The camera's digital circuitry (unintentional radiator) is covered by SDoC, and the SDoC responsible party must be located in the US (2.909(b)); for the imported private-label unit that is us unless the factory has a US party. Grantees must designate a US agent for service of process (2.911).
value.bad_labs_rule: Since Sep 2025 the FCC bars test labs and TCBs tied to prohibited entities (Covered List, Entity List, etc.); ask which lab tested the grant. Covered List also bars Hikvision/Dahua video equipment and (since Mar 2026) foreign-made routers; a dash cam is not a router, but avoid any Hikvision-made platform.

battery_shipping.value: Supercapacitor (EDLC) at or under 0.3 Wh is not subject to IATA/ICAO DG rules (Special Provision A186/361); a dash-cam supercap is typically far below this, so it ships as general cargo by express or air. A Li-ion dash cam ships under UN3481 (PI 967 Section II); many DDP lines surcharge or refuse battery cargo, and Li-ion degrades in parked-car heat.

prop65.value: Businesses with fewer than 10 employees are exempt by law, but retailers and marketplaces can require warnings by contract; the brand owner selling under its own name is the responsible party once over 10 employees. PVC cables can contain DEHP. Ask the factory for a Prop 65 / RoHS / REACH test report; add a CA warning at checkout if any listed chemical is above safe harbor.

prop65.source: p65warnings.ca.gov FAQ; compliancegate guide via search

compliance.other: CE/RoHS claims are irrelevant in the US except as quality signals. Camera recording laws (audio consent by state) belong in the manual. No safety certification needed for a 5 V device; the hardwire kit touches vehicle wiring, so include a fuse and low-voltage cutoff.

landed_estimates.finding: At the full STARVIS 2 4K+2K supercap spec ($53-75 FOB), landed cost is about $100-127 against a ~$105 retail price, because the 37.5% tariff stack applies. Only the $30-40 FOB tier lands at $64-81. Either pick a $35-45 factory model and prove its sensor, or reprice toward ROVE's $149.99. Rerun economics.py with these inputs before G2 for product 2.

extender.why: No listing matches the spec (3-panel rigid board, 20-in fold), so it is a semi-custom build from trading companies. The kit is bulky, so air costs $25-76 per kit. HTS is ambiguous (27% vs 52.5%), there are patents to design around, and timing is tight against Jan 4 and Chinese New Year. No certification needed.
extender.riskiest_step: Getting a production batch that matches an approved sample on board rigidity and the 20-inch fold. If the fold fails, both the USPS cost and the air-freight cost jump. Verify on the sample and again by photo/video before the balance is released.

dashcam.why: Many stock OEM models at MOQ 1-20 with 7-day lead times, light and dense freight, and the supercap avoids battery DG rules. Hard parts: sensor and spec claims are often false, FCC ID must match the exact unit, generic apps rate poorly (Viidure 4.0-4.4 from ~26-28K ratings; Kacam ~2.1, RoadCam 2.2), firmware support and tech-support returns, and the 37.5% tariff squeezes the $105 price.
dashcam.riskiest_step: Sample verification: confirm the real sensor (IMX678/675 via footage tests and a teardown photo), the supercap, the FCC grant for that exact model, and app reliability before paying for a batch. A wrong pick here means returns and support load at launch.

recommended_routes.extender: Samples from h6 + h9 by express, then a 15-20 kit first batch by express or DDP air (whichever quotes lower all-in, with true declared value), Dhruv ships by USPS. Then a 100-200 kit sea reorder (LCL or Matson DDP sea) placed before CNY with a third-party PSI.
recommended_routes.dashcam: Sample 3 stock models (BEPO ZD72S IMX678 supercap; one $35-45 tier such as Tengyue S856 or Fisang; Zhongxiang IMX675) plus fccid.io checks. Then a 15-20 unit neutral-box batch by express; buy branded microSD cards in the US. Logo, box and app branding only at the 200+ reorder by sea or DDP sea.
